text: This slice evaluates package BOOKING_MATCH itself, on the version it holds and through the embedded Drools kit, inside its own worker on queue rwb-decision, and publishes the outcome; the treatment state and the booking difference stay with rwb-treatment, the task and the route move with rwb-case, and the posting and TreatmentBooked with rwb-payment.
why: The Work Package places the story in rwb-decision with DP-04 and a C dependency on this service's own rule-package contract, so the slice decides rather than only stores, while DP-04 keeps the evaluation in one service and the registry story keeps governance central.
read: Work Package B2-P7-021 story line; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-04 and R5.4; RWB-E2-007 sections 4 and 12; P7 context pack slide 27.
confirm: Solution architect with the decision service owner and the registry owner
impact: Medium: the boundary is written once and every consumer maps the outcome to its own state, so a later move of the evaluation changes one service and no business value.

text: The six legacy published interfaces become REST operations on the per-service bases of DP-13 with one hop, a 2 s timeout and a fake: the ALS batch status and the account snapshot under RWB-P2-E2007-CON, the approved-not-booked read and the booking and difference write under the treatment contract, and the task request, the parameters and the lists under the case contracts. The decision code and the outcome values come from LOV-DECISION and the reference lists in force, the account facts of the business date sit in inputs_ref, the difference terms and the unbooked accounts sit in actions, the read filters are businessDate, treatmentId, caseId and outcome with a page of 50, and MSG-GEN-006 keeps its id with a placeholder text.
why: No source enumerates the target operations, payloads, decision code, snapshot shape or message text, and the legacy story fixes only the in-process signatures and the two endpoints.
read: RWB-E2-007 sections 11, 12 and 14; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 and T3.2; FSD P7 v3 A2.3; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-06, DP-07, DP-11 and DP-13.
confirm: Solution architect with the owners of rwb-integration, rwb-treatment and rwb-case and the reference-data owner
impact: Medium: the shapes become contract and reference data, so a later change is a contract version or a reference row and no scenario changes.

text: One rwb.decision.BookingDecisionMade.v1 is published per treatment and business date on rwb.decision.events.v1, keyed by treatmentId, carrying treatmentId, caseId, businessDate, one outcome of BOOKED, NO_BOOKING or TERMS_DIFFER, the row ID, the package code and version, the difference terms, the accounts without a booking and the decided time; TreatmentBooked and CaseStateChanged stay with rwb-payment and rwb-case.
why: The decision must leave the service that made it before the treatment is booked, and no source names the event; the P7 ownership rows name only EV-08, EV-09 and EV-30.
read: RWB-E2-007 sections 4, 12 and 17; Template and Rules v1 R4 and R5.5 DP-09 and DP-14; P7 context pack ownership rows and the shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1.
confirm: Solution architect with the event platform owner and the consumers
impact: Medium: the event is the only coupling to the three consumers, so a renamed event is a contract change in one place and no business value moves.

text: This story is the secondary rwb-decision slice of RWB-E2-007: it owns no legacy acceptance criterion, its fragment carries an empty acs list, its nine criteria are new and test only the decision, the record, the event, the gates and the read, and the metadata rows stay exactly as the Work Package fixes them, with Depends on (build) empty and RWB-P2-E2007-CON as the only contract dependency, while the seven platform H rows and the four consumed contracts of the pattern table are named in sections 3, 12.2, 12.8 and 13 and built against their fakes from Day 1.
why: Only step D1 may change the plan, and the patterns the Work Package fixes add rows the story line does not carry; naming them where they are used keeps the metadata exact and the dependency visible.
read: Work Package B2-P7-021 story line; Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R5.7 rules 2 and 8; P7 context pack ownership rows.
confirm: Solution architect with the delivery lead and the owners of the platform contracts
impact: No behaviour change; ready to start stays Day 1 because every H is a wave 0 platform contract and a C never blocks.

text: The story names the database login only as 'the rwb-decision login (DP-02)' and leaves the name to the ACE team, because no source gives it.
why: Template and Rules R4 and DP-02 fix one login per service and name none of them, and a story may not invent a credential name.
read: Template and Rules v1 R4 and R5.5 DP-02; P7 context pack naming rules.
impact: Low: the login is provisioned with the schema and nothing else depends on the spelling.

text: The story owns no legacy acceptance criterion and its eleven legacy test case IDs are kept in the order the Work Package fixes, with the Covers column naming this slice's new criteria and the rules they prove; the legacy level System maps to Component, Access to Contract and Resilience to NFR, and the -ITG copies belong to RWB-ITG-E2007-ITG.
why: The Work Package fixes acs empty and the eleven legacy test cases, and Template and Rules R7.2 s16 requires a Level column with values the legacy story does not use.
read: Work Package B2-P7-021 story line; RWB-E2-007 sections 7 and 16; Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s16.
impact: Low: the legacy criteria stay proved by the slices that own the treatment, the case, the payment and the screens, and no test case ID is added or dropped.

text: The event-started BookingConfirmationWorkflow runs on queue rwb-decision with the timezone Asia/Bangkok, one run per business date, a second start refused with MSG-P2-006, a failed gate retried on the next AceDataReady for the date, no fallback Schedule, and the flag off stops the start while the records already written stay readable.
why: The legacy story fixes the trigger and the rerun and no source fixes the timezone, the overlap and catch-up policy, a fallback sweep or the flag-off answer.
read: RWB-E2-007 sections 3, 4, 5, 12 and 13; Architecture v5 slide 44 through the P7 context pack; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-10.
confirm: Solution architect with the workflow platform owner and the platform administrator
impact: Low: the run stays one per business date either way and the values are configuration, so a later change touches no scenario.

text: No reconciliation_result table is created in rwb_decision: the counts of a run and the outcomes of a date are served from decision_log_entry on the read of 12.1, and the REC-03 break list is built by rwb-reporting from the published events, with DF-OPS-118 to DF-OPS-129 carried as values until that owner names its read model.
why: TSD P7 v2 declares no such table, DP-17 removes the data lake and moves reporting to rwb-reporting read models, and a story may not create another service's report table.
read: RWB-E2-007 sections 4, 5, 11 and 14; TSD P7 v2 T3.1; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-17 and DP-09.
confirm: Solution architect with the reporting owner and the data steward
impact: Low: the counts remain readable from the records and the report is a consumer of the events, so no business value moves.
